displayName: Deploy freshness — main merged but not deployed

conditions.displayName: Deployed commit drifted from GitHub main

conditionMatchedLog.filter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND (jsonPayload.event_type="deploy_freshness_drift" OR jsonPayload.event_type="deploy_freshness_repo_unreachable" OR textPayload:"deploy_freshness_drift" OR textPayload:"deploy_freshness_repo_unreachable")

documentation.content:
The hourly /regression deploy-freshness check found that what is SERVING is not what is on GitHub `main`.

Two events trip this policy:

- `deploy_freshness_drift` — main is ahead of the deployed commit by more than DEPLOY_FRESHNESS_MAX_HOURS (default 2h). The merge happened; the deploy did not.
- `deploy_freshness_repo_unreachable` — GitHub returned 404 for the repo. The repo was renamed/moved, or the token lost access. This is the FC-081 failure mode itself.

Why this policy exists: the build-failure alert watches builds that START. A build that never starts fires no failure alert. FC-031 sat undeployed 11 days behind a red build; FC-081 sat undeployed 16 days because a repo rename detached the Cloud Build trigger and no build ever ran.

Triage:
  # what is serving
  curl -s https://options-wheel-strategy-799970961417.us-central1.run.app/health | jq .git_commit
  # what should be serving
  git ls-remote https://github.com/memon1987/agentic_options_wheel refs/heads/main
  # did a build even run?
  gcloud builds list --limit=5
  gcloud beta builds triggers list

If no build ran for the merge commit, the trigger is detached — repoint it (this is what FC-081 fixed) rather than deploying by hand.

Note: the check reports `warn`, never `fail`, when GITHUB_TOKEN or GIT_COMMIT is unset, and on any transient GitHub error — so this policy does not fire on a GitHub outage.
